question.text: What percentage of the US hen flock will be sexed with in-ovo sexing technology in Q1 2027?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the percentage of the US' hen flock that was sexed with in-ovo technology according to official Innovate Animal Ag reporting as of Q1 2027.
question.fine_print: If Q1 2027 reporting is not released before July 2027, or If Innovate Animal Ag significantly changes its criteria such that previous reporting is not comparable, this question can be resolved by another credible source if it is comparable. Otherwise, the question will be **annulled**.

research:
I checked the resolution source, Innovate Animal Ag's (IAA) blog posts from 2025 and 2026, and recent trade news. IAA's latest figure for US adoption is "1%", and none of its reports so far gives the US number more precisely than that. Nothing settles the question yet.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-07 (data as of 2026-06-01): IAA's market penetration report, "Updated July 2026", says current US penetration "remains under 1%". Producers covering "over 4%" of the US commercial layer flock have announced full transitions as their old flocks retire. IAA "opted not to make a numerical forecast for the US market". It counts hens in production that were sexed in-ovo over a rolling 18-month window, using data supplied by the technology vendors. [IAA report](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast)
- 2026-10-05: IAA's Q3 2026 quarterly roundup, the latest official statement, says: "The United States is currently at 1% adoption, and will hit 4% as committed producers complete their transitions." [IAA Q3 2026](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-quarterly-roundup-q3-2026)
- I found no data file or dashboard behind these figures. The US number appears only as rounded text.
- Timing: IAA's annual reports have used data dates of April 1, 2024, April 1, 2025 and June 1, 2026, and the 2026 report came out in July. Quarterly roundups usually appear around the end of each quarter (Q1 2026 was published March 31). A "Q1 2027" figure is therefore most likely to come from the Q1 2027 roundup, around late March or early April 2027. The 2027 annual report could arrive after the July 2027 cutoff.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing is settled. The official value is about 1%, sometimes worded as "under 1%". Most of the 4% committed is still to come, and IAA says it will arrive as flocks turn over, roughly every 18 months.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-18: Cal-Maine says bird flu (HPAI) hit a Florida site and it will cull 1.4M laying hens plus 360K pullets. Its flock is about 48M hens. This mainly changes the denominator, the total US flock. [GlobeNewswire](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/11/18/3405662/0/en/Cal-Maine-Foods-Reports-Positive-Test-Result-for-Avian-Influenza-at-Florida-Facility.html)
- 2026-10-05: NestFresh has sexed 1.2M chicks in-ovo and expects 1.5M by end-2026. Orbem machines are running in two US hatcheries, with a third due in 2027. Orbem said "an announcement from one of the big retailers" was expected "very soon". I found no such announcement as of today. [IAA Q3 2026](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-quarterly-roundup-q3-2026)
- 2026-09-09: Hy-Line runs AAT's Cheggy machines in Iowa and Texas, but Cheggy only works on brown-egg layers, and about 90% of the US market is white layers. Vital Farms birds arrive in early 2027, and Kipster's own brand launches in early 2027. AAT says big US retailers will not pay extra for the technology. United Egg Producers (UEP) says it will adopt when "economically and operationally feasible." [AgFunderNews](https://agfundernews.com/in-ovo-sexing-hits-40-penetration-in-the-eu-what-will-it-take-to-crack-the-us)
- Current Vital Farms FAQ: it will adopt in-ovo sexing in "late 2026" with Hy-Line, with birds on farms in "early 2027". It expects "the majority of our hens" by 2028, which is later than the "by 2027" target IAA reported in December 2025. Vital's network had over 10M hens in 2025, about 3% of the US flock. [Vital Farms](https://vitalfarms.com/learn/faqs/what-happens-to-male-chicks/), [IAA 2025 recap](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-2025-review)
- 2026-06/07: NestFresh's entire portfolio is now in-ovo sexed, after more than 800K chicks. [IAA Q2 2026](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-quarterly-roundup-q2-2026)
- 2026-03-31: Sauder's is adopting in-ovo sexing for several specialty lines using Hy-Line and Cheggy, with rollout due by August 2026. Evermore Pet Food plans a full switch by end-2026. [IAA Q1 2026](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-quarterly-roundup-q1-2026)

## 4. Base rates and trend
- April 2024: US at 0%, with no installations.
- Q1 2025: under 1% of a 310M-hen flock, with the first chicks delivered in December 2024 (from the question background).
- June 2026: under 1%. October 2026: "1%".
- So the figure has grown by less than 1 point in about 18 months. My own rough check: NestFresh's 1.5M chicks by end-2026, divided by about 300M hens, is about 0.5%. Kipster, Sauder's and Evermore add small amounts.
- In the EU, penetration rose about 6 points per year (34% to 40%). But that was driven by laws, which the US does not have.
- Seasonality: none to speak of. The figure moves in steps as flocks are replaced. The main variable is the denominator, which falls when bird flu culls are heavy (typically in the fall and winter migration season). This series has no earlier years to compare against for the November-to-May period.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on this question. None of the markets supplied with the question is relevant: the "Flock" ones are about Flock license-plate cameras.
- IAA's only expert outlook: 4% "as committed producers complete their transitions", with no date attached and no numerical US forecast.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Late 2026 to early 2027: Hy-Line begins sexing chicks for Vital Farms, and the first birds reach farms in early 2027. They would only partly count toward a Q1 2027 figure.
- Early 2027: Kipster launches its own brand.
- Q4 2026 roundup (around early January 2027) and Q1 2027 roundup (around late March or early April 2027).
- A possible big-retailer commitment, which Orbem hinted at. Even if it happens, it would take more than 18 months to show up in the share of hens in production.
- The EGG SAVE Act tax credit for buying machines (status not checked).
- Bird flu culls shrinking the total flock, as with Cal-Maine on 2026-11-18. A smaller flock slightly raises the percentage.
- The 2027 annual IAA report, which may be published after July 2027.

Innovate Animal Ag (IAA) currently puts US in-ovo sexing penetration at about 1%: "under 1%" in its July 2026 report and "1%" in its October 2026 roundup. I found no IAA figure published after that.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-07 (report data as of 2026-06-01): IAA's "Market Penetration and Forecast" report says US "current penetration remains under 1%". It also says producers representing "over 4%" of the US commercial layer flock have announced full transitions as their existing flocks retire. IAA chose not to make a numerical US forecast. [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast)
- Q1 2025 (earlier report, published 2025-05-15): penetration was under 1% of a 310 million-hen flock. [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast-2025)
- Report timing matters. The 2025 edition used Q1 data and came out in May. The 2026 edition used data as of June 1 and came out around July. If the 2027 edition follows the 2026 timing, it may arrive near or after the July 2027 cutoff, which would trigger the backup-source or annulment clause.
- IAA's method for the EU: hens counted in production over an 18-month layer cycle, based on supplier-reported data. The report does not describe a separate method for the US.
- I found no CSV or JSON data file behind the IAA page. It is a narrative report.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. The latest official value is about 1%, or "under 1%".
- 2026-10-05: IAA's Q3 2026 roundup says "The US is at 1% in-ovo sexing adoption," with a forecast of 4% "as committed producers complete their transitions." No date was given for reaching 4%. [IAA Q3 2026](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-quarterly-roundup-q3-2026)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-18: Cal-Maine is culling about 1.4 million hens and 360,000 pullets after a bird flu (HPAI) outbreak in Florida. This affects the size of the flock that penetration is measured against. [GlobeNewswire](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/11/18/3405662/0/en/Cal-Maine-Foods-Reports-Positive-Test-Result-for-Avian-Influenza-at-Florida-Facility.html)
- 2026-10-01: NestFresh says it has in-ovo sexed 1.2 million chicks and expects about 1.5 million by end-2026. [Nombase](https://www.nombase.com/newswire/2026/10/01/nestfresh-reaches-major-humanely-hatched-milestone-sparing-12-million-male-chicks), [IAA Q3](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-quarterly-roundup-q3-2026)
- 2026-09-09: AgFunderNews reports:
  - Vital Farms' in-ovo sexed birds (Hy-Line hatchery, AAT's Cheggy machines) are scheduled to reach its farms in **early 2027**, with "the majority of our hens" from this process by 2028.
  - Retailers are "not willing to pay any extra."
  - The United Egg Producers trade group backs adoption only "when it is economically and operationally feasible."
  - Kipster plans to launch its own brand in early 2027.
  - [AgFunderNews](https://agfundernews.com/in-ovo-sexing-hits-40-penetration-in-the-eu-what-will-it-take-to-crack-the-us)
- In 2025, IAA said Vital Farms' network had over 10 million hens, roughly 3% of the US table-egg flock. [IAA 2025 recap](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-2025-review)
- 2026-07: Orbem has machines running in 2 US hatcheries and a third planned for 2027. Orbem said it expects "an announcement from one of the big retailers very soon." I could not confirm that any such announcement has happened. [AgFunderNews](https://agfundernews.com/orbem-begins-us-rollout-of-mri-based-in-ovo-sexing-tech)
- 2026-06: NestFresh says 100% of its laying flock is now in-ovo sexed. [IAA Q2](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-quarterly-roundup-q2-2026)
- The US now has 6 machines: 3 Cheggy units at Hy-Line, 2 Orbem, and 1 Seleggt Circuit at Hendrix in Nebraska. [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast)
- 2026-02: Sauder's became the fourth US adopter, for its specialty lines. [IAA Q1 2026](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-quarterly-roundup-q1-2026)
- I found no new commodity producer or retailer commitment from Q4 2026.

## 4. Base rates and trend
- US values so far: 0% before December 2024, under 1% in Q1 2025, under 1% (about 1%) in mid-2026. That is a gain of well under 1 percentage point a year so far.
- The EU took about 5 years to reach 15%, rising from 34% (revised) to 40% between April 2025 and June 2026, about +6 points in 14 months. Switzerland and Norway moved quickly once their few hatcheries converted. [IAA](https://innovateanimalag.org/market-penetration-forecast)
- Flock size: USDA reports 319 million table-egg layers on 2026-10-01, total layers up 4% year on year. I could not fully check the table values in the raw file. At that size, 1% is about 3.2 million hens. NestFresh's 1.5 million chicks alone is about 0.5%. [USDA NASS](https://esmis.nal.usda.gov/sites/default/release-files/796112/ckeg1026.txt)
- Penetration lags hatchery throughput because new hens replace retiring flocks over about 18 months or more. Vital Farms birds arriving in early 2027 would add little by Q1 2027.
- Seasonality: none in the penetration ratio itself. HPAI losses, which tend to rise in autumn and spring migration, can shrink the denominator. There is not enough history for a multi-year seasonal comparison.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on this question. None of the markets supplied with this request are related.
- IAA's only forward statement is that the US will reach about 4% once committed producers finish their transitions. It gives no date. [IAA Q3](https://innovateanimalag.org/blog/in-ovo-sexing-quarterly-roundup-q3-2026)
- Vital Farms expects most of its hens to be in-ovo sexed by 2028. The 2025 IAA recap had said by 2027. [AgFunderNews](https://agfundernews.com/in-ovo-sexing-hits-40-penetration-in-the-eu-what-will-it-take-to-crack-the-us)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- About early January 2027: IAA's Q4 2026 roundup and 2026 yearly recap, possibly with an updated US figure.
- Early 2027: first Vital Farms in-ovo sexed pullets placed on farms; Kipster brand launch.
- Possible big-retailer announcement (Orbem's hint), and Omegga and MatrixSpec launches in late 2026 or early 2027.
- Third Orbem US installation in 2027. EGG SAVE Act tax-credit legislation is still pending.
- About April 2027: IAA's Q1 2027 roundup. The 2027 market penetration report is possibly May to July 2027.
- HPAI culls through winter and spring 2026-27 change the flock denominator.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** The Q1 2027 IAA roundup is likely published in late March or early April 2027, about 4 to 5 months from now. Resolution is around 2027-05-31.

(b) **Latest known value:** IAA's Q3 2026 roundup (2026-10-05) says the US is at "1%" adoption. The June 2026 data said "under 1%".

(c) **If nothing changed:** about 1%, or possibly worded as "under 1%", which a resolver might read as about 0.5 to 0.9.

(d) **If the current trend continued:** About 1 to 2%.
- Hens already sexed in-ovo: NestFresh about 1.5M, Sauder's specialty lines perhaps about 1M, plus Kipster and Evermore in small amounts.
- New in early 2027: the first Vital Farms birds start arriving, perhaps 0.5 to 2M by the data date.
- That totals roughly 3 to 5M hens out of about 290 to 300M (a little lower after bird flu culls), or about 1 to 1.7%.
- IAA rounds to whole numbers, so "1%" or "2%" is most likely.

(e) **Historical variation:** The figure moved from 0% to "1%" over about 2 years, less than 1 point per year. A move of more than 1 to 2 points in 5 months would be unusual.

(f) **Expert and market expectations:**
- IAA: "4% as committed producers complete their transitions", with no date attached. That is clearly beyond Q1 2027 given 18-month flock turnover.
- There are no relevant markets.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- *Low:* Vital Farms is delayed, IAA uses stricter counting, and the report reads "under 1%", which the resolver records as 0.5.
- *High:* IAA counts committed or placed pullets more generously, a large producer starts placing birds early, and heavy bird flu culls shrink the total flock, so IAA reports 3%.

**Tails:**
- Percentile 1 (0.3): a report saying "under 1%", interpreted as a low fraction of a percent.
- Percentile 99 (4.5): a report quoting the full committed 4% as already achieved.
